summary: Kittitas County lookout on Bald Mountain: a 1931 tower and cabin, a 38-foot L-4 tower from 1955, removed in 1972; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 38-foot L-4 tower (1955) that replaced a 44-foot light steel tower with log cabin (1931)
facts.status_note: The L-4 tower was removed in 1972; the sources read do not describe what remains

events.note: 44-foot light steel tower with an accompanying log cabin, per the register
38-foot L-4 tower about one mile southeast of the summit
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: 44-foot light steel tower and log cabin built in 1931, replaced by a 38-foot L-4 tower one mile southeast of the summit in 1955
evidence.quote: This 44' light steel tower along with an accompanying log cabin, built in 1931, were replaced by a 38' L-4 tower 1 mile southeast of the summit in 1955.

evidence.supports: tower removed in 1972 per the register
register places the lookout in the Wenatchee National Forest
forest-lookouts list places the peak in the Snoqualmie National Forest
a patrol point two miles west of the summit
evidence.quote: There was also a patrol point 2 miles west.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Bald Mountain located in Kittitas County

sources.title: Bald Mountain Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Forest name conflict: the register says Wenatchee National Forest and the Forest Lookouts list says Snoqualmie National Forest. The story reports both and does not choose. The WillhiteWeb 'Bald Mountain' page covers a different peak near Lake Kelcema (4,760 ft, Everett Herald 1927 scouts' lookout) and was not used. Access and present condition are unknown; the Forest Lookouts entry gives no dates. Web search budget for this run ran out before the searches for this tower, so the story rests on the cached pages only.
